sampleSlides.title: How to build habits that actually stick
sampleSlides.body: A ten-slide guide to the small, compounding routines that quietly change everything.

sampleSlides.title: Motivation is a terrible strategy
sampleSlides.body: Motivation is a feeling, and feelings come and go with the weather. You can't schedule inspiration or borrow tomorrow's energy today. Systems don't care how you feel on a Tuesday — that's why they win.

sampleSlides.title: Start absurdly small
sampleSlides.body: Two push-ups. One page. One sentence. Small enough that skipping it feels sillier than doing it. Every tiny repetition is a vote for the person you're trying to become.

sampleSlides.title: Anchor to what already exists
sampleSlides.body: After morning coffee, I read for ten minutes. After I brush my teeth, I write one thing down. Stack the new habit on an old, automatic one — the old cue does the work your discipline can't.

sampleSlides.title: Design the environment
sampleSlides.body: Willpower is finite; friction is forever. Put the guitar on the stand, hide the snacks, lay out tomorrow's clothes tonight. Make the good choice the easy one and let the room do the heavy lifting.

sampleSlides.title: Track, don't judge
sampleSlides.body: Data over drama. A missed day is a data point, not a verdict on your character. Mark the box, keep the scoreboard honest — what you measure gets managed, what you judge just gets avoided.

sampleSlides.title: Never miss twice
sampleSlides.body: One off day is a life happening. Two in a row is a pattern forming. The rule isn't to be perfect — it's to come back fast. Recovery, not perfection, is the actual skill.

sampleSlides.title: Reward the process, not the outcome
sampleSlides.body: Celebrate showing up, not the number on the scale. Outcomes are slow and unfair; the process is the only thing you control today. Make finishing the rep feel like the win.

sampleSlides.title: You do not rise to the level of your goals. You fall to the level of your systems.
sampleSlides.body: Goals are the direction. Systems are the vehicle. A great goal with a broken system will strand you every time. Build the system first. — James Clear

sampleSlides.title: How to build habits that actually stick
sampleSlides.body: A ten-slide guide to the small, compounding routines that quietly change everything.

sampleSlides.title: Motivation is a terrible strategy
sampleSlides.body: Motivation is a feeling, and feelings come and go with the weather. You can't schedule inspiration or borrow tomorrow's energy today. Systems don't care how you feel on a Tuesday — that's why they win.

sampleSlides.title: Start absurdly small
sampleSlides.body: Two push-ups. One page. One sentence. Small enough that skipping it feels sillier than doing it. Every tiny repetition is a vote for the person you're trying to become.

sampleSlides.title: Anchor to what already exists
sampleSlides.body: After morning coffee, I read for ten minutes. After I brush my teeth, I write one thing down. Stack the new habit on an old, automatic one — the old cue does the work your discipline can't.

sampleSlides.title: Design the environment
sampleSlides.body: Willpower is finite; friction is forever. Put the guitar on the stand, hide the snacks, lay out tomorrow's clothes tonight. Make the good choice the easy one and let the room do the heavy lifting.

sampleSlides.title: Track, don't judge
sampleSlides.body: Data over drama. A missed day is a data point, not a verdict on your character. Mark the box, keep the scoreboard honest — what you measure gets managed, what you judge just gets avoided.

sampleSlides.title: Never miss twice
sampleSlides.body: One off day is a life happening. Two in a row is a pattern forming. The rule isn't to be perfect — it's to come back fast. Recovery, not perfection, is the actual skill.

sampleSlides.title: Reward the process, not the outcome
sampleSlides.body: Celebrate showing up, not the number on the scale. Outcomes are slow and unfair; the process is the only thing you control today. Make finishing the rep feel like the win.

sampleSlides.title: You do not rise to the level of your goals. You fall to the level of your systems.
sampleSlides.body: Goals are the direction. Systems are the vehicle. A great goal with a broken system will strand you every time. Build the system first. — James Clear

sampleSlides.title: How to build habits that actually stick
sampleSlides.body: A ten-slide guide to the small, compounding routines that quietly change everything.

sampleSlides.title: Motivation is a terrible strategy
sampleSlides.body: Motivation is a feeling, and feelings come and go with the weather. You can't schedule inspiration or borrow tomorrow's energy today. Systems don't care how you feel on a Tuesday — that's why they win.

sampleSlides.title: Start absurdly small
sampleSlides.body: Two push-ups. One page. One sentence. Small enough that skipping it feels sillier than doing it. Every tiny repetition is a vote for the person you're trying to become.

sampleSlides.title: Anchor to what already exists
sampleSlides.body: After morning coffee, I read for ten minutes. After I brush my teeth, I write one thing down. Stack the new habit on an old, automatic one — the old cue does the work your discipline can't.

sampleSlides.title: Design the environment
sampleSlides.body: Willpower is finite; friction is forever. Put the guitar on the stand, hide the snacks, lay out tomorrow's clothes tonight. Make the good choice the easy one and let the room do the heavy lifting.

sampleSlides.title: Track, don't judge
sampleSlides.body: Data over drama. A missed day is a data point, not a verdict on your character. Mark the box, keep the scoreboard honest — what you measure gets managed, what you judge just gets avoided.

sampleSlides.title: Never miss twice
sampleSlides.body: One off day is a life happening. Two in a row is a pattern forming. The rule isn't to be perfect — it's to come back fast. Recovery, not perfection, is the actual skill.

sampleSlides.title: Reward the process, not the outcome
sampleSlides.body: Celebrate showing up, not the number on the scale. Outcomes are slow and unfair; the process is the only thing you control today. Make finishing the rep feel like the win.

sampleSlides.title: You do not rise to the level of your goals. You fall to the level of your systems.
sampleSlides.body: Goals are the direction. Systems are the vehicle. A great goal with a broken system will strand you every time. Build the system first. — James Clear
